title: Classification decision record
description: The recorded EU AI Act triage of one AI system or model: the question set and version it was answered against, every answer with its article and meaning, the indicative scope, operator roles and risk classes with their reasons, the high-risk screen with the Art. 6(3) condition and the explicit profiling flag, the reviewer, the date, the legal-review state and the events that re-open it.
$comment: AI Governance Engineer templates and schemas library, v1. CC BY 4.0 (attribution: Jorge García Aibar). Produced by https://aigovernanceengineer.com/toolkit/ai-act-triage from chapter 18 of the Body of Knowledge. The outcome is indicative: an engineer's reading, not legal advice and not a conformity claim; counsel confirms the reading. x-evidences names the obligations a field or record helps evidence: an illustrative mapping, not a claim of conformity.

$schema.description: The URI of this schema, so a record says what it claims to be.

kind.description: Record kind. The triage refuses to re-open a file of any other kind.

version.description: Major version of the record format.

record_id.description: Identifier of this decision, stable for the same system and date (for example "cdr-2026-09-24-cv-screen-02").

system.description: The AI system or model the decision is filed against.

name.description: Name of the system or model.

registry_id.description: Id of the entry in the AI system register, so the record files next to it.

intended_purpose.description: What it is used for, by whom and in which context. The classification follows the intended purpose; a change of purpose re-opens the record.

question_set.description: The versioned question graph the answers were given against.

version.description: Semantic version of the question set. A new major version changes a rule, a question's meaning or an option value.

as_of.description: Date the question set reads the law as of.

basis.description: The legal text read, as amended.

answers.description: Every visible question that was answered, in the order asked, with the article it rests on and what the answer means.

question.description: Question id, stable within a major version of the question set.

article.description: The article the question rests on.

values.description: Option values chosen (one for a single-choice question).

labels.description: The options as the reader saw them.

means.description: What each chosen answer means, in the chapter's terms: the reason behind the answer.

outcome.description: The indicative outcome, recomputed from the answers whenever the record is re-opened.

scope.description: Whether the Act reaches the system or model on these answers. Out of scope, no role or class is given.

scope_reasons.description: Why, with the article, for every scope rule that held.

roles.description: Indicative EU operator roles for this system. Roles name tasks, not organisations.

role.description: Role id, as in the EU role table (roles dataset).

article.description: Where the Act defines the role.

reasons.description: Why the role follows from the answers.

classes.description: Indicative risk classes (rungs) and the GPAI track. Several can apply at once.

class.description: Class id, as in the obligation register's system classes, plus minimal.

article.description: The article the class rests on.

applies_from.description: First date the class's duties apply, where the chapter gives one.

reasons.description: Why the class follows from the answers.

high_risk_screen.description: The high-risk screen as the chapter's illustrative record states it: the Annex III area, the Art. 6(3) condition relied on and the explicit profiling flag.

annex_i.description: Annex I coverage of the product.

annex_iii_areas.description: Annex III areas the intended purpose falls in.

profiling.description: Whether the system profiles natural persons; null when not asked or not settled. Profiling makes an Annex III system high-risk whatever condition is claimed.

high_risk.description: Whether a high-risk class (Annex I or Annex III) follows.

open_points.description: Decisions or checks still missing. A record with open points is a draft.

notes.description: Consequences to act on (for example a FRIA, a registration, a notification clock).

rationale.description: The outcome in one paragraph, plus the reviewer's note.

reviewer.description: Reviewing role or forum. Roles, not personal names.

legal_review.description: Whether counsel has confirmed the reading. The engineer builds the evidence; counsel confirms the obligation was read correctly.

triggers.description: Events that should re-open the record.

review_by.description: Latest date for the next review.

notice.description: The fixed notice: indicative, not legal advice and not a conformity claim.

link.description: The link that reproduces the triage (the answers travel after #).

extensions.description: Organisation-specific fields. Validators ignore their content; keep evidence-bearing fields in the core record.
